questions.text: When SNAP is checked, must the visitor still enter household size and monthly income before receiving an eligible result?
questions.rationale: The page lists all three inputs (L7), but SNAP makes a household eligible regardless of income (L12) while the result must state an applied monthly limit (L13).

options.label: Keep unspecified
options.detail: Extract the SNAP override without asserting which fields are required; flag this as unresolved for downstream design.

options.label: Size only
options.detail: Require household size to display its limit, but do not require income when SNAP is checked.

options.label: All inputs
options.detail: Require size and income even when SNAP is checked.

questions.text: How should the check handle missing, zero, negative, fractional, or nonnumeric household size or income?
questions.rationale: L7 names the fields and L10-L11 define size-based thresholds, but no validation or invalid-input behavior is stated.

options.label: Keep unspecified
options.detail: Do not invent validation or error messaging; leave invalid-input handling unresolved.

options.label: Block invalid
options.detail: Require positive whole-number household size and nonnegative numeric income; block checks with missing or invalid values.

options.label: Provide rule
options.detail: Specify a different validation and error-handling rule in free text.

verdict.bugTitle: Eligibility checker approves income above displayed monthly limit
verdict.rootCause: The eligibility decision is treating an income that exceeds the stated monthly limit as eligible.
verdict.suggestion: Fix the income comparison so a one-person household with no SNAP and monthly income of $2,462 is not eligible when the applied limit is $2,461.
verdict.oneLiner: The checker says the household is eligible even though $2,462 is above its displayed $2,461 monthly limit.

verdict.bugTitle: SNAP household incorrectly marked ineligible above displayed income limit
verdict.rootCause: The eligibility calculation is applying the $2,461 monthly limit to this SNAP household and returns Not eligible for the entered $2,462 income, rather than the required Eligible result.
verdict.suggestion: Review the SNAP eligibility rule for a one-person household at $2,462 monthly income, then add a regression test for this boundary scenario.
verdict.oneLiner: The eligibility check marks the entered SNAP household as not eligible even though the recorded scenario requires an Eligible result.
